feature: official grpc-cpp max concurrent streams connection scaling

scope.direction: official grpc-cpp client to netz server
scope.placement: streams 1 and 2 on connection A; stream 3 on connection B
scope.lifecycle: all three streams remain open through their first response, then the client half-closes all three and requires OK

toolchain.source_build_probe: current PATH selected /nav_env/.pixi/bin/clang without C++ standard headers; the conformance run reused the already-built fixed-revision official client above

implementation.peer_address: HTTP/2 Connection.peerAddress and gRPC ServerConnection.peerAddress return the remote endpoint retained by std.Io.net.Stream for both cleartext and TLS
implementation.server_duplex: movable server duplex handles share one role-specific owner count and one frame reader; sibling HEADERS are HPACK-decoded once and queued DATA is routed by stream id
implementation.layout: the existing client owner counter is shared by the mutually exclusive client/server connection role, preserving Connection size at 2032 bytes
implementation.fixture: a dedicated connection-scaling module accepts two connections, serves two live RPCs on A and one on B, and verifies the two real peer endpoints differ
implementation.runner: max_concurrent_streams_connection_scaling is part of every h2c/TLS reverse matrix

results.reverse_matrix: 25 scenarios per transport, 50 total, passed over h2c and TLS
results.connection_scaling_h2c: first two peer addresses equal and third nonempty/different; all three streams finished OK
results.connection_scaling_tls: first two peer addresses equal and third nonempty/different; all three streams finished OK with certificate verification and ALPN h2
results.forward_matrix: netz client to grpc-cpp server complete h2c/TLS matrix plus same-SharedChannel A-to-B failover passed

remaining_gap: The standardized max-concurrent-streams connection-scaling case is externally covered. Broader repeated and fault-injected multi-connection distributions remain separate stress evidence.
